text:
kim: Quick sync: we've been seeing long-tail starvation on the continuous-batcher under mixed workloads. I want to propose surfacing lightweight backpressure hints from the queue to admission so we can do soft-deprioritization instead of hard preempts.
arpit: Sounds promising. What do you mean by hints vs. full-blown metrics?
kim: Not full timers per-tenant. Three compact, hot-path-friendly signals: (1) queue_depth_by_size (small/med/large buckets), (2) kv_cache_pressure (approx count of hot K/V entries pinned), (3) a short-decay eviction counter. Use these to compute a tiny headroom score that travels with the reservation token.
soraya: cheap to compute? we mustn't add allocs on enqueue.
kim: implementation idea: maintain per-tenant counters stored in an arena so updates are atomic ops (fetch_add + occasional read). decay can be a multiply by decay_factor executed on read, not on every enqueue. store enum+byte on token.
mike: eviction counter worries me. we've observed eviction storms when large tenants cause lots of kv churn; naive reaction could oscillate.
kim: agree. we should use exponential decay (half-life ~100ms) and combine signals with hysteresis. soft_hold only activates if eviction_score AND kv_pressure exceed thresholds. and add cool-down windows to prevent flip-flop.
elaine: what's soft-deprioritization behavior? do we stop batching entirely? that might increase RNG latency.
kim: soft_hold reduces batch eligibility: prioritize fastpath and microbatch lanes, disallow bulk-coalesce for a short period. It isn't a preempt; it's a suggestion that lowers the tenant's chance to be coalesced into large batches.
arpit: can we encode the hint in the reservation token rather than changing enqueue proto? token already flows downstream, so minimal code touches.
kim: exactly. token gains a small enum: NORMAL|SOFT_HELD|FORCED and a score byte. Admission sets it, batcher reads it. no API surface change for customers.
soraya: rollout? I want telemetry-first.
kim: proposed rollout: 1) telemetry-only: emit candidate signals and decisions (shadow mode) but do not alter behavior. 2) opt-in for selected tenants via feature flag. 3) global opt-in with conservative defaults. 4) tuning experiments (hysteresis, thresholds).
telemetry-bot: kim configured metric stream: continuous-batcher.signals.{queue_bucket,evict_score,kv_pressure,soft_hold_eval} -> datadog (low-card).
elaine: make sure we don't add tenant_id tags on high-volume metrics. use size buckets and occasional sampled tenant ids for deep-dive logs.
soraya: shadow-mode is crucial: compute soft_hold decisions and log predicted vs actual, with tiny sample rate. then we can validate before flip.
arpit: SLO safety: we need an automatic circuit breaker. If P99 generation latency or error rate increases beyond X% in rolling 5m after enabling, auto-disable soft_hold globally for 10m and page ownership.
mike: tests: unit tests + integration replay. I'll add a fuzz harness that replays a set of production traces (including runaway-tenant traces) to measure throughput, tail latencies, and eviction churn with/without soft-hold.
kim: also add a shadow-apply scenario in canary where decisions are computed and logged but not applied, and a small subset of tenants opt in.
elaine: doc changes: console should expose per-tenant toggle, heuristic recommendations, and a one-click rollback. include a small playbook: when tail p99 rises, disable, collect trace, investigate.
soraya: observability detail: emit path tag (fastpath|microbatch|bulk) and sample batch_sizes when soft_hold applied. low-card metrics only; detailed traces go to long-tail store.
arpit: implementation notes: keep hot-path ops to O(1) atomic ops and avoid floating-point multiplies on enqueue. compute decay on read path or in background sampler. use integer fixed-point for score.
mike: what thresholds? default conservative values: eviction_score>8 (with decay), kv_pressure>100, and queue_bucket==large. we can tune after telemetry.
kim: owner matrix: I'll write the RFC and diagrams. arpit: you'll take token + admission plumbing. soraya: telemetry and dashboards. mike: test harness and traces. elaine: rollout playbook and circuit-breaker.
kim: timeline: RFC by EOD tomorrow, instrumentation PR the following week, shadow-canary in two weeks.
elaine: one more ask: include a stability test that checks for oscillations over a 30m simulated run. we don't want soft_hold causing new eviction storms.
arpit: agreed; include hysteresis window (min 500ms) and a backoff multiplier.
soraya: and add an opt-out per-tenant config for Private deployments behind a feature gate.
kim: perfect. I'll include a telemetry table and sample dashboards in the RFC. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
